hook: The floor that becomes a trap
aciklama:
Earthquakes rarely kill people directly - buildings do. Here is the hidden physics of why some towers fall while others survive.

#shorts #engineering #earthquake #science #howitworks

sahneler.metin: An earthquake almost never kills you. The building does.
One weak floor collapses, and the floors above crush it.
Engineers call this soft story failure, and it takes just seconds.
But why does one floor fail first?
The ground shakes side to side, not up and down.
Open ground floors, like parking levels, have too few walls.
Modern towers are built to bend, some on giant rubber bearings.
The safest building in an earthquake is one designed to move.

vaka.ders: modern codes require ductile frames and base isolation
vaka.yanilgi: People fear the shaking, but most earthquake deaths come from collapsing buildings — especially ones with open, weak ground floors.
vaka.tartisma: Should cities force owners to retrofit soft-story buildings, even when it's expensive?
